title: The queue arms accepted candidates before integration certification is green
status: confirmed in owned local fixture; no product fix
expected: Only certified integration accepts ordinary candidates; pending/uncertified wait. Proven red repair stays separately allowed.
actual: Unmodified script main issues one --auto merge command for pending, uncertified and certified fixtures; red control issues zero. All four successful corrected runs exit0/stderr0.
rootCause: The consumer tests only state===red, so all other certification states fall into queueAcceptance and landing.
impact: A merge may precede the full validation boundary required by the comment at458-464. This can add work before integration is known green; branch protection still applies to candidate checks.
recommendation: Require positive certified state for normal acceptance, define pending/uncertified reporting and retain the explicit red repair proof.
regressionTest: Pending and uncertified arm0; green arm1; red only a proven full-green level repair can arm. Check actual main sequence with owned command ports.
relationship: Independent of ORCH-05 missing CI planner gates and C9 local publication equivalence. Both concern evidence, but this cause is consuming a four-state certification as a boolean red/non-red.
limits: queueAcceptance is a port fixture returning a valid accepted candidate; classifier/order/checks/main are unmodified. No real merge or provider operation. First failed isolation attempt made four synthetic-path GitHub GET404; retained separately, discarded as target evidence. Corrected tests use owned PATH gh and blocked Git.

title: Incremental journal import permanently skips events published late with an older source timestamp
status: confirmed in owned local fixture; no product fix
expected: A previously unseen remote event remains importable regardless of when its author timestamp falls relative to unrelated local events.
actual: With local event timestamp200 and newly published remote event100, real reader plus real runJournalStep incremental imports0 and leaves old absent. Full-mode control imports1 and retains it.
rootCause: The cursor is the maximum occurredAt of every local event; remote filtering uses occurredAt>=cursor rather than publication position or unseen identity.
impact: Cross-machine recovery/ownership/journal evidence can remain absent on every warm boot, despite being durably present on the ref. No malformed data required.
recommendation: Track publication cursor/ref ancestry or import by stable event identity; do not treat an event clock as append order. Preserve idempotent replay.
regressionTest: Import newer local state, publish an older remote event afterwards, then run two incremental boots; new identity must arrive once. Include full control and equal timestamp case.
relationship: Distinct from PROP-JOURNAL01 torn-tail append and state drain retirement. Existing publication merge is append-only, but event occurrence timestamps are not a publication cursor.
limits: Own source uses typed in-memory local rows and a fake Git port returning actual NDJSON; no network/SQLite needed. Existing real-owned Git journal tests passed separately. No private journal or actual missed user event inspected.

title: Startup generation validation depends on check response order instead of all check verdicts
status: confirmed in owned local fixture; no product fix
expected: A generation with a failing relevant check stays non-green regardless of the array order; green represents the required evidence set.
actual: Real runForgePhase with actual GenerationsRepo and owned SQLite memory database stores green/success for [failure,success] and red/failure for [success,failure] at the same candidate SHA.
rootCause: Each individual check overwrites the same generation-wide validationState/ciResult row. There is no grouping or policy-aware fold.
impact: Reconstructed checkpoint can be reported green while another check failed. Forge branch protection is independent; no actual bad merge demonstrated.
recommendation: Aggregate the current check set using required policy and completion semantics before updating generation validation once; retain individual CI rows.
regressionTest: Permute failing/success/pending checks at same SHA; aggregate verdict must remain stable and non-green whenever required evidence fails/is absent.
relationship: Different from ORCH-05 CI job omission and USAGE-02 latency attribution; all rows are present here but projected into a last-write generation scalar.
limits: Current host binds createForgeSeam which lists check runs, so this path is reachable. Own fake forge delivers typed responses; actual SQLite repository is exercised with a minimal owned table, not the complete production migration stack.

title: A merged PR can mark a different checkpoint head integrated through ref-name fallback
status: confirmed in owned local fixture; no product fix
expected: A merge fact is associated only with the checkpoint head it proves; reusing a ref name does not prove the new head merged.
actual: Actual phase plus real GenerationsRepo stores new-sha checkpoint as integrated at old-merge for a merged PR whose head is older-sha, provided ref names match. Matching-head control also integrates.
rootCause: Head-SHA lookup falls back to ref name without requiring equal head or ancestry before markIntegrated. Integration-evidence skips already integrated rows.
impact: A seam that includes merged PRs can permanently bless newer work with older merge evidence.
recommendation: Require exact checkpoint head evidence or explicit ancestry proof and correct target generation; retain merged facts without attaching them to a newer head.
regressionTest: A reused branch advances after an older PR merged. Reconciliation must retain the new checkpoint as unintegrated; same-head merged control integrates.
relationship: Related to reconstruction truth and prior CP-10 integration wiring, independent of ref deletion/expected-tip races. No new cleanup mutation is exercised.
limits: Important counterevidence: shipped host forge-seam.service.ts187 lists state=open, so this exact merged response is not produced by the current host adapter. It is a real public-seam/library branch defect, tested through its declared contract; no present live-host incident or default-triggered loss claimed.

title: GitHub integration adapter reports merged without validating the merge response body
status: confirmed in owned local fixture; no product fix
expected: A successful CLI/HTTP transport is checked for an affirmative merge fact and nonempty commit SHA before returning status merged.
actual: Real adapter with injected exec returns status merged, mergeSha empty, unchanged base for successful command JSON {merged:false,sha:""}. Affirmative merged:true control returns expected merge SHA.
rootCause: The adapter checks run.ok but reads only body.sha and unconditionally returns merged, ignoring body.merged and malformed/empty evidence.
impact: An adopter of this adapter can persist an integration event from a non-merge result. The downstream merge-step treats merged as sufficient to upsert/markIntegrated.
recommendation: Validate positive response fields and return a typed refusal/failed outcome when merge evidence is absent; do not infer semantic success from command success.
regressionTest: Transport success with merged:false, empty body, invalid JSON and missing SHA must not yield merged; affirmative valid response remains success.
relationship: Distinct from MAINT-04 ignoring delete result and RECLAIM-02 ignoring expected tip. CP-10 establishes the engine is not currently wired into the production candidate publisher, limiting current reach.
limits: Injected exec only, no GitHub behavior observation and no real merge. The JSON fixture verifies parser/result contract rather than claiming a particular live HTTP status. Production-engine integration remains CP-10 limitation.
